text:
maria: Heads up — ran into a tenant incident this morning where the primary regional model (gptx-13b-prod) got saturated and kept queuing. We fell back manually to a cheaper compatible variant, but it was messy. Thinking about an automated, cost-aware variant fallback that considers tier + region. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

ajay: I saw the alert. Is the ask to auto-fallback when utilization > X, or to proactively route low-tier traffic to cheaper variants during surges?

maria: Primarily automated on-saturation. For non-enterprise tenants prefer cheaper fallbacks; for enterprise keep strict SLA and maybe only fallback to verified low-cost replicates. Also want telemetry so we can see who fell back and why.

sofia: We should classify fallback reasons explicitly in metrics: fallback_reason={capacity,quota,latency,degraded_model}. Right now logs are just "fallback" which is useless.

ryan: Agreed. Also we need to account for cache warming impact — new variants often have cold KV cache and increased latency. Any fallback policy must allow a short pre-warm window or limit QPS to avoid thrashing.

ajay: Implementation sketch: add a routing policy block per tenant that supports a "capacity_threshold" trigger and an ordered list of compatible variants with cost metadata. Example config (internal):

```
routing_policy:
  tenant: example-tenant
  priority_by_tier:
    - tier: free
      primary: gptx-13b-prod
      fallbacks:
        trigger: capacity_threshold
        threshold: 0.85
        allowed_variants:
          - gptx-13b-quant4-compat
          - gptx-7b-compat
        prefer_lower_cost: true
        prewarm_seconds: 30
    - tier: enterprise
      primary: gptx-13b-prod
      fallbacks:
        trigger: capacity_threshold
        threshold: 0.95
        allowed_variants:
          - gptx-13b-prod-hot
        prefer_lower_cost: false
```

maria: Love that. We should expose an API flag so SDKs can opt-out per call: prefer_compatible_variants=false. Also console level override to force fallback behavior per route.

sofia: For telemetry we'll emit these labels: tenant_id, region, primary_model, fallback_variant, fallback_reason, latency_percentile_post_fallback, cost_delta_tokens. Add a daily aggregation: fallback_rate_by_tenant and fallback_heatmap_by_region.

ops-bot: [alert] region-us-west model pool saturated: gptx-13b-prod (85% qps burst) — auto-mitigation not configured for tenant 'acme-inc'.

ryan: For rollout UX: console should show a mini-playback for a tenant: before/after latency, tokens, and cost. Maybe a toggle: "simulate fallback" so account owners can preview impact.

ajay: One tricky bit — model equivalence. Need a small metadata registry that marks variants as "functional_compatibility: high/medium/low" and lists which layers/hyperparams change KV semantics. Fallback should only choose variants with compatible KV semantics or do transparent KV translation (hard).

maria: Ops question — if we fallback by region, do we ever cross-region fall back? e.g., route us-west traffic to eu-central fallback when us-west saturated but eu has capacity? Legal/regulatory says no for some tenants. So policy must be region-aware: allow_cross_region: true/false per tenant.

sofia: Also add metric labels for cross_region=true so we can alert on cross-region fallbacks.

ajay: Proposed API changes: POST /v1/routing/policies to create tenant policy; response includes effective_policy_id. Add per-call header: X-Redwood-Prefer-Fallback: low_cost|strict_sla|no_fallback.

maria: UX: in Console > Routes > Route detail show: current primary, fallback chain, recent fallback events (clickable), and an "audit" button to see full logs (redact PII). Also an easy switch: "Enable auto-fallback (recommended for non-enterprise)" with a brief explainer.

ryan: For safety, implement graceful demote window: when we switch a percent of traffic to fallback, ramp for 30s -> 3m -> evaluate metrics -> continue or rollback. Same as canary.

ajay: Telemetry hooks: emit an event type route.fallback.started and route.fallback.completed with outcome=success|rollback and metrics attached. That will let Optimize run cost/quality regressions automatically.

maria: Action items: Ajay prototype routing policy + header in dev cluster (ETA 2w). Sofia add metrics + dashboard panels (fallback_rate_by_tenant, fallback_latency_impact) and a heatmap (ETA 1w). Ryan help design prewarm + canary ramp strategy and failure modes (ETA 1w). I'll draft console copy and UX mocks.

sofia: I'll also add a kpi alert: if fallback_rate_by_tier.free > 5% sustained for 1h, ping eng-platform and product.

ajay: I'll stash a small PoC in eng-runtime that simulates prewarm by replaying last 5 KV slices to fallback instance. Will add feature flag: routing.auto_fallback_enabled.

maria: Great. One more: add cost cap per-tenant for fallbacks (monthly token cost delta limit). If hit, stop falling back to cheaper but expensive variants. Need to calculate cost_delta in real-time.

ryan: Okay. I'll draft the canary playbook and failure detection thresholds this afternoon.

maria: Thanks team. Keeping this thread as the source of truth for the experiment. If anyone wants to join the sync, ping me. :rocket:
